_comment: The machine-readable export boundary: every path downstream projects consume, grouped by HOW it reaches them (which determines how changes propagate). Validated by .github/scripts/check-exports.js in qa.yml: every path must exist, and every raw-URL self-reference in the tree must point inside one of these paths. Anything not listed here is internal to this repo and safe to move.

inherited-rules.mode: fetched live by raw URL at session start — changes propagate immediately

installed-tooling.mode: installed via the plugin marketplace / SessionStart hook — propagates to the next session for projects carrying .claude/hooks/session-start.sh, otherwise on the env cache rebuild (~weekly); versioned by git SHA

copied-scaffolding.mode: copied into projects at bootstrap — snapshots that drift by design; /refresh-repo detects drift

referenced-docs.mode: read on demand via links — no copy, no install

domains._comment: The LOGICAL view, orthogonal to categories (which encode propagation): domain → compartment → paths. `names` lists the domains; each record under `paths` names its domain and compartment, so a compartment's paths are the records that name it. A compartment is the swappable unit — replace its file set honoring its interface and nothing outside it moves. Rendered visually at docs/site/logical-map.html; boundaries and swap procedure in MAINTAIN-REPO-USER-INSTRUCTIONS.md → Domain Boundaries. Validated by check-exports.js: a record naming a domain not listed here fails, and so does a listed domain no record names.

swap._comment: Swap classes over the domain view. PERMANENT paths evolve via PR and are never wholesale-replaced — this covers directives/ and the exported standards under docs/standards/, since both carry blocking criteria; PERMANENT_DOMAINS names domains that are permanent in their entirety (the whole meta domain): every record in such a domain is permanent by derivation in check-exports.js and does NOT carry `swap: permanent`, which marks only the permanent paths outside such a domain (an unknown domain name, or a `swap: permanent` record that overlaps a path a permanent domain already covers, fails the check). ORCHESTRATORS (`swap: orchestrator`) are permanent AND define the flow/interfaces their components must fit — a new component does not exist until its orchestrator sequences it. A record with no `swap` is swappable within its compartment's interface.

classes._comment: Durability classes over the exported set — WHAT KIND of thing each file is, and therefore what happens to it as models improve. Independent of `swap` (which says whether a path may be replaced) and of the domain (which says what it belongs to). Every record under `paths` names exactly one class, and check-exports.js refuses a class not defined here, so this view cannot rot the way an unchecked diagram would. Drawn at docs/site/logical-map.html, which build-logical-map.js generates from this file.

standard.label: Standards
standard.blurb: State blocking criteria a change must satisfy. Model-independent: a smarter model still has to meet them.

orchestrator.label: Orchestrators
orchestrator.blurb: Define the flow and the interfaces components must fit. A component does not exist until its orchestrator sequences it.

behavioral.label: Behavioral scaffolding
behavioral.blurb: Tells a model HOW to act. The only class that decays as models improve — audit it whenever the model tier changes.

mechanical.label: Mechanical enforcement
mechanical.blurb: Runs with no model in the loop. Immune to model change; the backstop when scaffolding is trimmed.

artifact.label: Artifacts
artifact.blurb: Fill-in templates and scaffolds. Consumed by a project, never executed here.

reference.label: Reference
reference.blurb: Read on demand. Explains and illustrates; binds nothing on its own.

paths._comment: One record per exported path: its domain and compartment (the logical view), its durability class, and, where it has one, its swap class. Keyed by path; a key ending in '/' is a directory and covers every file under it. Validated by check-exports.js: every path must exist, every record must name a domain listed under `domains`, a compartment, and a class defined under `classes`, and every shipped file under an exported root must fall inside a record (the reverse pass).

externals._comment: Vendor-owned capabilities this system depends on but does not contain — we hold only the sockets. To swap a vendor: rewire the listed socket files, never fork the vendor's code. serves = a domain.compartment some record under `paths` names. sockets = the files here that name/enable/configure it (must exist; validated).

anthropic-skills.note: Adoption covers doc-comp's dependencies only (the built-in docx and pdf skills its SKILL.md names). skill-creator stays rejected (considered -> skill-creator); the other sibling skills are recorded in considered -> out-of-domain.

considered._comment: Native capabilities evaluated by the upkeep mandate (CLAUDE.md -> Purpose) and NOT adopted wholesale. externals records what we depend on; this records what we looked at and declined, so an audit reads the verdict instead of re-deriving it. verdict: borrowed (an idea taken, the implementation stays) | rejected (does not fit) | deferred (fits, not yet done). stays = the path that keeps the job; must exist (validated). names = for an entry recording several natives under one key, the manifest or inventory name of each, so the parity diff can match every one of them.

commit-commands.rationale: Creates commits/PRs; /commit-chk verifies BEFORE a push. Complementary, not overlapping.

feature-dev.rationale: Generic explore/architect/review flow. Its clarifying-questions phase is /diagnose's job (plugins/directives-toolkit/commands/diagnose.md: one question at a time, 2-3 approaches, then specs/<slug>/brief.md), and its build phase is /sdd-loop's, which is bound to the imported directives as its constitution.

claude-md-management.rationale: Its claude-md-improver skill grades CLAUDE.md A-F; that rubric is copied into /audit-repo, so nothing loads the skill at runtime. Recorded under the PLUGIN name, which is what a marketplace manifest advertises and therefore what the parity diff sees. Its /revise-claude-md command (update CLAUDE.md with the session's learnings) is not adopted: /learn (plugins/directives-toolkit/commands/learn.md) appends typed, confidence-scored lines to learnings.jsonl, latest-key-wins and validated by check-learnings.js, rather than adding prose to CLAUDE.md, whose rules are owner rulings and not a session's notes.

hookify.rationale: Its hooks add dirname(CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT) to sys.path then `import hookify`, which assumes the plugin root's basename is the package. The versioned install layout (hookify/0.1.0/) puts a version dir there instead, so all four registered hooks -- PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit -- fail with "No module named 'hookify'" on EVERY tool call. Not forkable (externals rule: rewire sockets, never fork vendor code). Revisit only if upstream stops assuming that layout; plugin-dev's hook-development skill covers the same authoring ground without hooks of its own.

skill-creator.rationale: Its eval MODEL (query + should-fire, scored over repeated runs) shaped the first local runner, which `claude plugin eval` has now replaced entirely. Its own runner is unusable: scripts/run_eval.py returns on the FIRST tool use of the FIRST assistant message, so any preamble reads as no-trigger -- it scored the known-good pdf skill 0.00. Nothing of it remains in the repo; kept as a rejected-with-reason so no audit re-adopts it for trigger testing.

fewer-permission-prompts.rationale: Built-in skill that mines transcripts for common tool calls and proposes an allowlist. Our allowlist is not discovered from usage - it is an owner ruling (global.md -> Scheduling Tools Never Prompt) admitting two classes only - the six scheduling tools and read-only tools that change nothing and return no outsider-written content - with recorded accepted residuals, deliberately excluding the riskier remote tools a usage-mined list would surface. Adopting it would widen the grant by exactly the mechanism the ruling rejects.

init.rationale: Built-in skill that writes a CLAUDE.md by reading the codebase. /new-repo writes one from templates/CLAUDE-template.md, which carries the imported directive URLs, the UI-test config table, the project-specific test scenarios table the ui-tester refuses to run without, and the reporting contract. A codebase-derived CLAUDE.md has none of those, and a new repo has no codebase to derive from.

claude-code-setup.rationale: Analyses a codebase and recommends Claude Code automations for it - hooks, skills, MCP servers, subagents. This fleet's automation set is not derived per codebase: /new-repo installs one standard (the workflow set, the composite actions, the Playwright kit, styles/, the marketplace + plugin enablement, and the SessionStart hook), and owner rulings decide what joins it. Per-repo recommendations are the per-project drift that standard exists to prevent.

session-report.rationale: Generates an explorable HTML report of session usage - tokens, cache efficiency, subagents, skills and the costliest prompts - from local transcripts. A usage report, the same job as receipts under out-of-domain, which this repo does not have. Recorded on its own because the name reads like a session summary: it is not a handoff, and /handoff-session stays delta-only (global.md -> Handoffs Carry Only What Dies With the Session).

code-simplifier.rationale: Anthropic plugin, plus the built-in /simplify skill. Used for per-file quality cleanup; /audit-repo keeps only what neither does - repo-wide directive drift, the CLAUDE.md grade, native-parity, and structural soundness across the tree.

artifact-design.rationale: Built-in skill; the design-side sibling of artifact-diagramming and dataviz, both already borrowed. Authority for any published Artifact's design pass. design.md defers to it the way it defers to the other two.

artifact-capabilities.rationale: Built-in skill defining the runtime capabilities a published Artifact may declare. Required reading before /doc-comp publishes its diff as an Artifact rather than writing an undeliverable local file.

lsp-plugins.rationale: The twelve Anthropic language-server plugins listed in names (liquid-lsp, in the same marketplace, is Shopify's and outside the parity pass). This repo is markdown, small Node scripts and YAML; a language server buys nothing over node --check and the existing validators. Recorded as one entry so a future parity pass does not re-derive twelve verdicts.

output-styles.rationale: explanatory-output-style and learning-output-style change how a session narrates. global.md -> Plain Language First and Say It in Verbs already own that, as owner rulings; a plugin that overrides them would contradict the directives.

claude-security.rationale: Deep vulnerability scan that also generates and applies verified patches, with hooks of its own. The security job is already delegated to Anthropic natives recorded in externals (security-guidance plugin + built-in /security-review), and the toolkit maintains no security reviewer for it to replace. A heavier scan-and-patch tier suits a project with application code; install it per project, not fleet-wide from here.

ralph-loop.rationale: A Stop hook blocks session exit and re-feeds the SAME prompt until the model emits a completion-promise string. /sdd-loop iterates over spec -> plan -> tasks artifacts with the imported directives as the constitution, so completion is decided by the directives' gates (tests, CI, review), not by a string the model chooses to print.

ralph-wiggum.rationale: The same plugin as ralph-loop, advertised under its older name by the claude-code-plugins marketplace. Same verdict and reason; recorded separately because the parity diff matches manifest names.

simplify.rationale: Built-in skill; already covered by the code-simplifier entry, recorded under its own name because the parity diff matches names. /audit-repo recommends it as a follow-up and never runs it itself, since it APPLIES fixes and audit-repo is findings-only.

loop.rationale: Built-in skill that re-runs a prompt on an interval. git.md -> GitHub API Quota Economy says never poll for CI, deploy, or PR status (webhook wakes instead), and CLAUDE.md -> Notifications forbids arming a timed check-in as a substitute for a subscription. A recurring prompt is the mechanism both rulings exclude.

cron-tools.rationale: Session-scoped tools that schedule a prompt to re-run on a cron schedule: the same mechanism as the loop skill, rejected on the same grounds (considered -> loop). git.md -> GitHub API Quota Economy says never poll for CI, deploy or PR status, and CLAUDE.md -> Notifications forbids arming a timed check-in as a substitute for a subscription, since a timer cannot know whether anything changed. A one-off follow-up the rules do allow uses send_later (externals -> ccr-harness-tools).

run.rationale: Built-in skill that launches and drives the app for a one-off look at a change. The ui-tester agent does a different job: it runs the project's Playwright suite against the URL CLAUDE.md names and writes the report the orchestrator reads, which is the evidence test.md asks for. Complementary, not overlapping.

project-artifact.rationale: Publishes a living project status page as a claude.ai artifact. This repo's published view is the logical map, generated from EXPORTS.json and checked in CI (build-logical-map.js --check) on GitHub Pages; a status page built from gathered state would be a second, unchecked view of the same repo.

playground.rationale: Generates single-file interactive HTML explorers. The logical map is the only interactive page here, and its behaviour is hand-written and held by the Repo Map UI Playwright suite; a generated explorer would carry none of those invariants.

out-of-domain.rationale: Natives listed in names, each serving a job this repo and its toolkit do not have. Plugins: agent-sdk-dev and mcp-server-dev (SDK or MCP server development), mcp-apps and mcp-tunnels (MCP app and tunnel work), claude-opus-4-5-migration (model migration), code-modernization (legacy modernisation), cwc-makers (hardware onboarding), math-olympiad (competition math), receipts (usage reports). Built-in skills: claude-api (API reference), keybindings-help (keybindings). anthropic-skills siblings of the adopted docx/pdf (externals -> anthropic-skills): built-in-browser, chrome-browser and computer-use drive a browser or desktop on the person's own machine, while this repo verifies UI with headless Playwright in CI (test.md); deep-research writes cited research reports, not repo changes; docs makes Claude Docs living documents, while this repo's documents are committed Markdown; google-workspace edits Google files; import-memory imports another assistant's memory, while project memory here is learnings.jsonl; morning renders a personal daily brief; pptx and xlsx make slide decks and spreadsheets, which nothing here produces. Harness tools: watch_url and unwatch_url receive artifact-service webhooks, and this repo publishes no artifacts it watches. Recorded as one entry so a future parity pass does not re-derive each verdict.

workflow-authoring.vendor: Anthropic (built-in skill and Claude Code tool)
workflow-authoring.rationale: The workflow-authoring skill and the Workflow tool it writes scripts for: a script that orchestrates many subagents in the background (code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows). Its shape fits qa-pipeline, a fixed multi-agent sequence, and it runs from the top level, which matters because sub-agent nesting is off in this cloud environment (TIME-SENSITIVE.md, Models & sub-agents). Rejected for its opt-in cost, not its fit: Claude may start a workflow only when the user opts in. The skill's own description says it is for a workflow the user already opted into and does not itself authorize running one; the docs make the opt-in the user's own typed request or ultracode, and in manual permission mode the launch also asks for approval on every run. /sdd-loop runs the pipeline itself after every task, unattended, so the pipeline cannot depend on a per-run opt-in. Resolution (owner-approved, 2026-10-11 audit, I-25): qa-pipeline becomes a top-level toolkit command instead. Re-judge if a plugin-shipped workflow can be started by a command without the user's per-run opt-in.

math-proof.rationale: Two skills that work a hard mathematics problem to a self-contained proof.md, solo or in rounds of judge and worker sub-agents. Out of scope: no job in this repo or its toolkit is mathematical proof. Recorded on its own rather than under out-of-domain because it arrived after that entry's audit.

plugin-authoring.rationale: Built-in skill that writes a mod - a pane, band, status line, toast or hook - as function hooks that hot-reload in the CURRENT session. The toolkit's guard hooks (the push and wait gates among them) must reach every session in every downstream repo, so they ship through the claude-directives marketplace as plugin files under plugins/directives-toolkit/hooks/; a session-local mod reaches no other session. plugin-dev stays the authoring authority (CLAUDE.md -> Toolkit changes).

messaging-channels.rationale: Chat-channel plugins in Anthropic's official marketplace, under its external_plugins/ directory, so not Anthropic-built and outside the parity pass's Anthropic-owned count either way. Out of scope: nothing in this repo or its toolkit talks to a chat channel. Owner ruling 2026-10-08: recorded as rejected so the ownership question does not recur on every audit.

ccr-session-mutators.rationale: Evaluated and kept behind a permission prompt, never pre-approved: each mutates or widens a session's reach (attaches a repository or registers its clone, spawns, archives, unarchives, interrupts, retags or renames a session). global.md -> Scheduling Tools Never Prompt lists the first five under what must keep prompting, and the same section says anything absent from `allow` prompts by default, which covers the other three; a session uses one only when the user asks for exactly that.

push-notification.rationale: Sends the person a desktop or phone notification. CLAUDE.md -> Notifications makes the PR subscription the wake channel: it is kept until merge and its events arrive in the session, and global.md -> Status Line on Every Stop reports status on a wake that already happens, never on an extra one. A push on top would add a second, unruled channel to the owner for events the subscription and the status line already carry.

code-review.rationale: The code-review plugin (plugins/code-review in both claude-plugins-official and claude-code-plugins): five Sonnet reviewers plus Haiku confidence scoring, posted with `gh pr comment`. Superseded by the built-in /code-review skill, which the directives already name (externals -> code-review-builtin). Its command is also called /code-review, so installing it would collide with the built-in the directives point at, and it drives `gh pr` subcommands that a web session's gh does not have (only `gh api` works there).

design.rationale: knowledge-work-plugins design (Cowork-first): /critique, /design-system, /handoff, /ux-copy, /accessibility, /research-synthesis, plus nine MCP connectors (Figma, Slack, Linear, ...). It audits and documents a design team's existing system and hands specs to developers. This fleet's design method is per-project and generative instead: /design-intake distils tokens.css + components.css and an approved reference page, design.md is the method, frontend-design builds, and check-contrast.js enforces WCAG contrast mechanically. No Figma or design team to hand off from.

engineering.rationale: knowledge-work-plugins engineering (Cowork-first): /standup, /review (a code-review skill also named code-review), /debug, /architecture, /incident, /deploy-checklist, plus ten MCP connectors (Slack, PagerDuty, Datadog, ...). Its review lane is already delegated to pr-review-toolkit and the built-in /code-review and /security-review through qa-pipeline; /debug and /architecture overlap /diagnose; /deploy-checklist overlaps /commit-chk and update-pages. Its code-review skill name would shadow the built-in /code-review the directives name.

plugin-management.rationale: knowledge-work-plugins cowork-plugin-management (listed as Plugin Management): create-cowork-plugin and cowork-plugin-customizer, both declaring that they need the Cowork desktop app, delivering a packaged .plugin file or editing mounted plugin directories. plugin-dev is this repo's authoring authority (CLAUDE.md -> Toolkit changes) and the toolkit ships as source in a marketplace, not as a .plugin file.

document-skills.rationale: The anthropics/skills marketplace's document-skills plugin bundles the xlsx, docx, pptx and pdf skills, which sessions already have built in as anthropic-skills (externals -> anthropic-skills). Installing it would load a second copy of the same four skills under another name.

productivity.rationale: knowledge-work-plugins productivity: a memory-management skill that writes working memory into CLAUDE.md and a memory/ directory, and a TASKS.md task tracker. This repo's compounding memory is learnings.jsonl, written by /learn as typed, confidence-scored lines and validated in CI; CLAUDE.md holds owner rulings, not session memory.

product-management.rationale: knowledge-work-plugins product-management: /write-spec (a PRD from a problem statement) plus roadmap, stakeholder, research, competitive and metrics workflows. The spec step is /diagnose -> /sdd-loop specify here, bound to the imported directives; the rest is product-management work this repo does not do.

vertical-plugins.rationale: Anthropic-owned business and industry plugins from the built-in anthropic-plugin-directory (~/.claude/plugins/plugin-directory-cache-v2.json): the knowledge-work-plugins entries that do not overlap the toolkit (design, engineering, plugin-management, productivity and product-management have their own entries), and every Anthropic-owned entry of the financial-services, claude-for-financial-advisors, claude-for-legal and life-sciences repositories. operations covers both the knowledge-work and the financial-services plugin of that name. Out of domain: none of these jobs (marketing, sales, finance, legal practice, HR, support, biomedical research, PDF annotation) exists in this repo or its toolkit. Partner-built entries in the same repositories (life-sciences' partner connectors, claude-for-legal's external_plugins/cocounsel-legal, knowledge-work's partner-built/) are outside the Anthropic-owned count. Recorded as one entry so a future parity pass does not re-derive each verdict.
